item.title: Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhen Bao

item.title: Identities of Representation of Lie subalgebras of the first Weyl algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.06305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a field. We study weak polynomial identities for pairs $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the first Weyl algebra over $F$ and $V$ is either a Lie subalgebra (under the usual Lie bracket) of $A$, or simply a vector subspace of $A$. Sometimes the weak identities of $(A,V)$, when $V$ is a Lie algebra, are called identities of representations of Lie algebras. Our starting point is the description of finite dimensional Lie algebras $L$ that can be embedded into the first Weyl algebra; this description was given by Rausch de Traubenberg, Slupinski and Tanas\u{a} in 2006. First we assume that $F$ is algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and describe a finite basis of the weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$ where $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$. In order to obtain such a basis we invoke theorems by Razmyslov and by Trishin concerning the identities of infinite dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. Afterwards we consider $L$ as a filiform Lie algebra together with its concrete realisation inside the first Weyl algebra. We produce a finite basis of weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$, assuming $F$ to be infinite. Finally we study the weakest form of identities for $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the $n$-th Weyl algebra and $V$ is just a vector space - its canonical generating vector subspace. We deduce a basis of the weak identities in this case as well, once again assuming $F$ to be an infinite field, with no restriction on its characteristic. The same result was recently obtained by Dotsenko and Lopatin in characteristic $0$ by different methods. Our methods are combinatorial, we also use the theory developed by Razmyslov, and the representations of the symmetric and the general linear groups and their duality. We employ the characteristic-free description of the invariants of the symplectic group given by De Concini and Procesi.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav Futorny, Plamen Koshlukov, Jo\~ao Fernando Schwarz

item.title: High-Degree Restricted Cohomology for $K(3;1)^{(1)}$ in Characteristics Five and Seven
item.description: arXiv:2611.06396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the high-degree restricted first cohomology of the positive subalgebra of the rank-one contact algebra in characteristics five and seven, with parabolically induced coefficients. In degrees from twice the characteristic through four times the characteristic minus three, each characteristic has six nonzero homogeneous components, of total dimension thirteen. The constituents include Frobenius twists of the natural horizontal module, represented by Cartier cocycles. PBW duality converts the calculation into bounded-degree homology, where the coefficient action couples the natural and cubic relation coordinates. The resulting modules determine the high-degree part of the coefficient cohomology used in the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre term $E_2^{0,1}$ for extensions of induced contact modules. In particular, extensions from the Steinberg induced modules vanish in these degrees.
item.dc:creator: Chao Ma

item.title: On Jordan nilpotency of index n in group rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.06587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $RG$ be the group ring of an arbitrary group $G$ over an associative and commutative ring $R$ with identity. In this paper, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for $RG$ to be Jordan nilpotent of index $n \geq 2$. In particular, we establish a connection between the study of Jordan nilpotency in group rings and the study of Lie nilpotency in these algebras. We also classify the Jordan nilpotency of $RG$, over rings of arbitrary characteristic, up to the index $6$.
item.dc:creator: Osnel B. Cristo, Mariana G. Cornelissen, Rodrigo L. Rodrigues

item.title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology. Using this topology, we establish a topological Mundici adjunction that restricts to an equivalence between topological MV-algebras and Mundici-fine abelian topological $\ell$-groups with a strong unit. Here, Mundici-fine means that the group topology is the finest $\ell$-group extension of its unit-interval topology. We also identify extremal $\ell$-group extensions under additional hypotheses, and establish a quasitopological correspondence clarifying the distinction between separate and joint continuity.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Meng, Lili Shen, Dexue Zhang

item.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=\kappa$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by G\"obel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Haruhisa Enomoto

item.title: The group of strong automorphisms of the differential field of transseries
item.description: arXiv:2611.06520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the group of strongly additive automorphisms of the differential field $\mathbb T$ of transseries as a non-trivial semidirect product. We show that this group is torsion-free and has trivial center, and that many naturally arising differential subfields of $\mathbb T$ are definably closed in $\mathbb T$.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries, Joris van der Hoeven

item.title: Quantum regularity of finite dimensional semisimple algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.21936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a necessary and sufficient criterion for a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ to admit a regular quantum commutative decomposition. We apply this characterization to group algebras and show that a finite group algebra admits such a decomposition if and only if the underlying group is a peak group, that is, a finite group whose irreducible character degrees have a greatest element with respect to divisibility. We investigate the structure of peak groups and establish several criteria for their solvability in terms of the prime divisors of their largest irreducible character degree. In particular, we show that several important classes of groups are peak groups, while supersolvability alone does not imply the peak property. Finally, we show how to construct a peak group from any finite group.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Bahturin, Lucio Centrone, Kau\^e Pereira

item.title: Exponent Profiles of Oscillatory Matrices under Matrix and Inverse Sparsity
item.description: arXiv:2609.35846v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the simultaneous half-bandwidths $p,q$ of a symmetric oscillatory matrix $A$ and its inverse. At order $n\ge2$, the possible pairs are $(1,n-1)$, $(n-1,1)$, and all pairs with $2\le p,q\le n-1$. Let $e_k(A)$ be the least positive integer $m$ for which all minors of order $k$ of $A^m$ are positive, and let $e(A)=\max_{1\le k<n}e_k(A)$. Put $a=\min\{p,q\}$ and $b=\max\{p,q\}$. At every feasible pair of actual half-bandwidths, \[ \max_A e(A)= \max\left\{\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor, n-a-\left\lfloor\frac{\max\{n-p-q,0\}}{b}\right\rfloor\right\}. \] We also determine the maximum of $\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}e_k(A)$ for every pair. When $p+q\ge n$, one realization maximizes all $e_k$ simultaneously. Write $A=U^T\Delta U$, with $U$ unit upper triangular and totally nonnegative, and $\Delta$ positive diagonal. Let $\ell(U)$ be the least number of elementary upper bidiagonal factors with positive parameters whose product is $U$. At fixed $(p,q)$, its minimum is $\max\{n-1,p+q-1\}$. One symmetric integer matrix of determinant one simultaneously attains this minimum, the maximum exponent, and the maximum exponent sum. We prove $\ell(U^{r+1})-\ell(U^r)=\#\{k:1\le k<n,\ e_k(A)>r\}$ for every integer $r\ge\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$, with the starting point optimal. With $\delta=\ell(U)-n+1$, the exponent sum satisfies $\delta\le n(n-1)/2-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}e_k(A) \le\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\delta$, with both constants sharp. The lower deficit bound is attained at every admissible factor count. Within the symmetric class, a total sum of $n(n-1)/2$ characterizes basic matrices. In the basic oscillatory class, without a symmetry assumption, a positive integer vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1})$ is realizable if and only if $f_k\le\max\{k,n-k\}$ and $f_k+f_{n-k}\ge n$ for $1\le k<n$, and $\lvert f_{k+1}-f_k\rvert\le1$ for $1\le k<n-1$. Explicit factor orders realize every such vector.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xie

item.title: Balanced subsets in root systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.11219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Balanced and well-balanced subsets of the set of positive roots of compact Lie algebras arise naturally in problems related to Hermitian and spin geometry. In this paper we compute the maximal and minimal size of well-balanced subsets in all simple root systems.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Moroianu, Paul Schwahn

item.title: Almost Symmetric Linear Arc Monadic Datalog and Transitive Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2606.24711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce $n$-almost symmetric Datalog and study $n$-almost symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog. We characterize the finite relational structures whose constraint satisfaction problem is solved by this Datalog fragment as those that can be primitive positively constructed from the transitive tournament on $n+2$ vertices. We also give characterizations in terms of a certain homomorphism duality (which we call $n$-fixed unfolded caterpillar duality) and in universal-algebraic terms (the existence of $k$-absorptive operations and of operations forming an elevator chain of length $n+1$). This article generalizes the results from Bodirsky and Starke about symmetric linear arc monadic Datalog.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Meyer, Florian Starke
